item.title: Kidnapped Mexican border town mayor found alive
item.description:
Kidnapped Mexican border town mayor found alive
He was kidnapped for several hours while traveling in the state of Zacatecas.ByALFREDO PEÑA Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 4:09 PM
Share
CIUDAD VICTORIA, Mexico -- The mayor of a Mexican border town was found alive Sunday after he was kidnapped for several hours while traveling in the northern state of Zacatecas, federal officials said.
Miguel Angel Almaraz was traveling with family and friends Saturday in a region that straddles the states of Zacatecas and San Luis de Potosi, when his car was intercepted by armed men, who took Almaraz and let his family go.
According to the Security Department of San Luis Potosi, Almaraz’s relatives were able to reach a town in that state, where they alerted authorities about the kidnapping.
Officials said that Almaraz was taken to the city of Zacatecas, where he was released by his captors. The case is under investigation.

Several drug gangs known for attacking civilians and politicians operate in the area where Almaraz was kidnapped Saturday, including the Jalisco New Generation Cartel and the Sinaloa Cartel. So far, authorities have not identified the perpetrators of Almaraz’s kidnapping.
Almaraz is the mayor of Rio Bravo, a municipality of about 110,000 people in Tamaulipas state. The city is located just seven miles (11 kilometers) from Mexico's border with Texas.
The mayor was imprisoned in 2009 on accusations of money laundering and stealing fuel but was acquitted six years later. Almaraz is a member of the conservative National Action Party, but has represented other parties in his political career, including the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution.

item.title: Saudi Arabia turns to Syria for help as fighting with Houthis escalates
item.description:
Saudi Arabia turns to Syria for help as fighting with Houthis escalates
Syria is preparing to send fighters to Saudi Arabia to support its escalating conflict with rebels in neighboring YemenByGHAITH ALSAYED Associated Press and SAMY MAGDY Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 12:00 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
DAMASCUS, Syria -- Syria is preparing to send fighters to Saudi Arabia to deploy along its border and potentially help it fight Iranian-backed rebels in neighboring Yemen, three officials with knowledge of the plans told The Associated Press.
Syrian military advisers have already deployed to Saudi Arabia, but no fighters have been sent to Yemen, according to a regional official and two Syrian officials, all of whom spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to comment publicly.
Officials in Saudi Arabia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Fighting escalated this summer in Yemen between the Houthi rebels and the government's Saudi-backed forces. The Houthis have also launched direct and deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia in what is the latest front in the regional conflict that began in February when the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran.
Syria, which has a supply of battle-hardened fighters after a long civil war, has so far stayed on the sidelines.
Saudi Arabia has an array of U.S.-supplied fighter jets and missile defenses but has been unable to defeat the Houthis in past rounds of conflict.
While Saudi Arabia's other allies have been reluctant to commit ground forces to its fight with the Houthis, the Syrian government is beholden to it. The Saudis provided funds to Syrian rebels during that country's civil war and have promised much-needed financial assistance for Syria's postwar reconstruction.
A Syrian official said that an initial force of about 600 Syrian special forces fighters is expected to be deployed to Saudi Arabia in the coming week.

item.title: Sudan’s military again detains International Criminal Court fugitive Haroun, lawyers say
item.description:
Sudan’s military again detains International Criminal Court fugitive Haroun, lawyers say
Sudan’s military authorities have once again detained Ahmed Haroun, a former senior Islamist official wanted by the International Criminal Court for atrocities in DarfurByYASSIR ABDALLA Associated Press and SAMY MAGDY Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 11:48 AM
SHENDI, Sudan -- Sudan’s military authorities on Sunday once again detained a former senior Islamist official who is wanted by the International Criminal Court over atrocities related to the Darfur conflict in the early 2000s, two defense lawyers said.
Ahmed Haroun, a senior security official during the rule of longtime dictator Omar al-Bashir, and later chairman of the former ruling National Congress Party, was detained in Sudan’s eastern province of Kassala, according to two lawyers on his defense team.
The lawyers, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren’t authorized to brief the media, said Haroun’s whereabouts were unknown.
Haroun was detained in April 2019 when a monthslong uprising forced the military ouster of al-Bashir and his government.
He had been detained along with the former president and other senior officials, including those who are wanted by the ICC, in a Khartoum prison. The military declined to hand them over to the international court.
The conflict in Darfur broke out when rebels from the territory’s ethnic central and sub-Saharan African community launched an insurgency in 2003, complaining of oppression by the Arab-dominated government in Khartoum.
Haroun was accused by the ICC of crimes against humanity and war crimes including murder, rape, persecution, forced transfer of the population and torture in Darfur at least between 2003 and 2004.
Haroun has denied the charges. He walked away from the prison after the facility was attacked in April 2024 during the war between the army and the notorious paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.

item.title: Turkey and Azerbaijan deny speculation of fraying relationship
item.description:
Turkey and Azerbaijan deny speculation of fraying relationship
The Turkish and Azerbaijani presidents have reaffirmed the countries’ close ties following speculation of souring relationsByThe Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 11:40 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
ISTANBUL -- The Turkish and Azerbaijani presidents reaffirmed their countries’ close ties Sunday in response to growing speculation of souring relations.
Turkey and Azerbaijan are traditional allies with deep cultural and ethnic ties and often describe themselves as being “one nation, two states.” But tensions have emerged recently following criticism in Turkey of Azerbaijan’s decision to ban hijabs in schools and over Baku’s growing ties with Israel.
“Our brotherhood transcends our shared language, history and culture," Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said, speaking at a joint news conference with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev in the city of Shusha.
"That is why we see Baku’s joy as Ankara’s joy and Shusha’s pride as the pride of our entire nation,” Erdogan added.
The rift became apparent after social media users in Turkey and some members of Erdogan’s Islamic-oriented ruling party criticized Baku’s decision in September to ban girls and teachers from wearing Islamic covering in schools. Erdogan’s government overturned a similar ban in Turkey after coming to power in 2003. The criticism drew anger in energy-rich Azerbaijan, which complained of interference even though Turkey’s government had made no official statement about the hijab ban.

item.title: South Africa's ANC is humbled by its worst election results as it continues its decline
item.description:
South Africa's ANC is humbled by its worst election results as it continues its decline
South Africa’s African National Congress is party facing its worst election results everByGERALD IMRAY Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 10:34 AM
Share
CAPE TOWN, South Africa -- South Africa's African National Congress party faced its worst election results ever Sunday and a new low point on its gradual decline in popularity as voters rebuked it for a failure to deliver basic services like water and electricity in towns and cities.
The once-dominant ANC — the party of Nelson Mandela — had received around 30% of the vote in Wednesday's local government elections with 99% of ballots counted. The final results were expected late on Sunday, according to the Independent Electoral Commission.
The ANC remained the largest party by total share in an election involving hundreds of parties, but the Democratic Alliance that is its main opposition had received around 25% of votes in the near-complete count.
That brought closer to reality the once-unthinkable notion that the ANC that led South Africa out of the white minority rule of apartheid and delivered freedom in 1994 under Mandela might one day not be its biggest party. It used to command 70% of the vote.
The ANC's popularity has declined for more than a decade. It won 45% support in the last local elections in 2021, the first time it had dropped below 50% in any election. In 2024 it then lost its Parliamentary majority for the first time in a national election, which brought about a coalition national government and a seismic shift in South African politics.
The ANC was on course Sunday for a steep drop of about 15 percentage points from the last local elections and the loss of approximately one-third of its support from five years ago.

item.title: Tens of thousands march in Amsterdam, pressing the Dutch government on Gaza and Israel
item.description:
Tens of thousands march in Amsterdam, pressing the Dutch government on Gaza and Israel
Tens of thousands of people, many dressed in red, have marched through Amsterdam, demanding the Dutch government take stronger action against Israel over GazaByMIKE CORDER Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 10:04 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
AMSTERDAM -- Tens of thousands of people, many of them dressed in red, marched through Amsterdam on Sunday in a mass demonstration aimed at pressing the Dutch government to take more decisive action against Israel over Gaza.
The organizers of “Red Line” demonstrations in the Netherlands called for measures including stricter trade sanctions on Israel, officially declaring that Israel’s actions in Gaza amount to genocide and halting all arms sales to Israel.
The Dutch branch of Amnesty International, one of the organizers, said in an online post that more than 200,000 people joined the march.
“What is happening there is inhumane,” Mike van Dongen said as he walked in the huge throng of people. He was critical of the Dutch government’s actions. “As far as I’m concerned, they are doing nothing,” he said. “They don’t dare take any serious steps.”
As the protesters marched along a normally busy Amsterdam street that was closed to traffic on Sunday, a man stood on a bus stop with a loudspeaker shouting, “Free, free Palestine!” Many of the marchers echoes his cry as they passed.
Israel strongly rejects suggestions it is committing genocide in Gaza in its military campaign that followed the attacks by Hamas-led militants in southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023. Militants killed around 1,200 people and took 251 hostages. Israel’s retaliatory offensive has killed tens of thousands of Palestinians and destroyed much of Gaza.

item.title: At least 21 dead after boat carrying migrants sinks off Senegal coast, interior ministry says
item.description:
At least 21 dead after boat carrying migrants sinks off Senegal coast, interior ministry says
At least 21 people died after a boat carrying migrants sank off Senegal's coast, according to the country's interior ministryByEVE BRENNAN Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 9:25 AM
Share
DAKAR, Senegal -- At least 21 people died after a boat carrying migrants sank off Senegal's coast, the country's interior ministry said on Sunday.
The ministry said in a post on X that as of Saturday evening one person had been found alive, and that teams had been mobilized to continue searching for any more possible survivors. It did not specify how many people were believed to have been on board.
The ministry said the boat sank off the coast of the town of Kébémer, north of Dakar. It added that Senegal’s interior minister will visit the site on Monday.
The Atlantic migration route from West Africa to Spain's Canary Islands is one of the deadliest in the world. At least 635 people died in the first five months of 2026, according to the Spanish rights group Walking Borders.

item.title: 2 trains crash in Egypt; 2 dead, more than 100 injured
item.description:
2 trains crash in Egypt; 2 dead, more than 100 injured
Egypt's railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance.ByThe Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 9:04 AM
Share
CAIRO -- Seven people were killed and over 100 others injured when two trains collided Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, the Chief Prosecutor’s office said in a statement. It also said the train’s conductor was among those killed.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 52 kilometers (32 miles) south of Cairo, when a train traveling to the southwestern Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the Transportation Ministry.
The Chief Prosecutor's office said late Sunday its investigators had arrived at the site. An inspection indicated that the crash took place when the Giza-Fayyoum train collided with the last carriage of the Cairo-Aswan train, that was stationary on the same track and traveling in the same direction, officials said.
Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system which has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years, the government announced modernization initiatives to improve its railways.
Ayman Gamal, a resident of Kafr Girza in al-Ayyat where the crash occurred, said people living nearby rushed to the scene, pulled out survivors and called ambulances,
Gamal said that he saw around 80 of the injured were taken by ambulances to nearby hospitals. Some passengers were trapped inside one of the carriages of the stationary train and were dead when they were pulled out, he said.

item.title: Tourists and locals recount fatal Krakow mass shooting that left Poland reeling
item.description:
Tourists and locals recount fatal Krakow mass shooting that left Poland reeling
Tourists and locals alike witnessed a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland, that left six people dead and 15 woundedByRAFAL NIEDZIELSKI Associated Press and CLAUDIA CIOBANU Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 8:21 AM
Share
KRAKOW, Poland -- Tourists and locals alike this weekend witnessed a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland, that left six people dead and 15 wounded.
The country’s second-largest city is in mourning after a 24-year-old man with far-right views opened fire in Main Square, a major tourist hub, Saturday afternoon. The gunman is in serious condition and also linked to the deaths of his sister and parents at his family home.
Witnesses in Krakow said the violent attack was so surreal, it felt like they were in a film. Polish leaders, visitors and locals praised police officers who shot and wounded the attacker.
Here’s a look at what the witnesses and others said:
— “We literally ran for our lives and managed to hide from the bullets flying around,” Marie-Ange Collaer, a visitor from Brussels, wrote on Facebook. “Lying on the floor in a shop like in a bad police movie whilst you hear bullets everywhere.”
— “We had just walked through the main square and heard the gunshots,” U.K. resident Neil Thaxton wrote on Facebook. “We thought it was fireworks then people started running, we went into a gift shop and the staff took us in the back of the shop and locked the doors and turned the lights off.”
— “In the face of the tragedy in Krakow, we saw the best in people: the courage of police officers, the dedication of paramedics, and the selfless help of ordinary people who rushed to save others," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote on X. "We are all deeply grateful to them.”

item.title: Israel’s president gives Eisenkot the first chance to form the next government
item.description:
Israel’s president gives Eisenkot the first chance to form the next government
Israeli President Isaac Herzog has formally given opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form the next governmentByGIOVANNA DELL'ORTO Associated Press and MELANIE LIDMAN Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 6:24 AM
Share
JERUSALEM -- Israeli President Isaac Herzog formally gave opposition politician Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form the next government Sunday evening.
Complex coalition negotiations still lie ahead, but it marked a significant step in the former military chief's effort to oust Israel's longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, after elections held in a deeply divided country. Israel remains scarred by the Hamas-led attacks of Oct. 7, 2023, and the multifront wars they triggered.
“I hope with all my heart that whatever government is formed will lead to unity, connection and healing among all segments of our people — for our very existence depends on it, and we have only one country,” Herzog said at the ceremony at the presidential residence in Jerusalem.
The announcement doesn't guarantee that Eisenkot will become the next prime minister. He has up to six weeks to form a coalition government by securing alliances, a daunting challenge because the Oct. 27 election gave neither his bloc nor Netanyahu’s a clear majority in parliament.
Herzog said that in consultations with the parties, a majority of members of parliament, known as the Knesset, supported giving Eisenkot this task.
At Sunday's ceremony, Eisenkot promised to give the country leadership that people can trust, that will act in the interests of the public and that represents all parts of society.
“An absolute majority of Knesset members representing the Israeli public support change,” he said. “I intend to navigate the situation with patience, humility, composure and a deep commitment to a Jewish, equal, liberal, and secure Israel.”
